kudos.m: An expression of approval and commendation.

kudu.m: Either of two spiral-horned antelopes of the African bush.

kudzu.m: Fast-growing vine from eastern Asia having tuberous starchy roots and hairy trifoliate leaves and racemes of purple flowers followed by long hairy pods containing many seeds; grown for fodder and forage and root starch; widespread in the southern United States.

kudzus.m: Fast-growing vine from eastern Asia having tuberous starchy roots and hairy trifoliate leaves and racemes of purple flowers followed by long hairy pods containing many seeds; grown for fodder and forage and root starch; widespread in the southern United States.

kumiss.m: An alcoholic beverage made from fermented mare's milk; made originally by nomads of central Asia.

kumquat.m: Small oval citrus fruit with thin sweet rind and very acid pulp.

kumquats.m: Small oval citrus fruit with thin sweet rind and very acid pulp.

kunzite.m: A pinkish lilac crystal form of the mineral spodumene that is used as a gemstone.

kunzites.m: A pinkish lilac crystal form of the mineral spodumene that is used as a gemstone.

kurrajong.m: Widely distributed tree of eastern Australia yielding a tough durable fibre and soft light attractively grained wood; foliage is an important emergency food for cattle.

kurta.m: A loose collarless shirt worn by many people on the Indian subcontinent (usually with a salwar or churidars or pyjama).

kurtas.m: A loose collarless shirt worn by many people on the Indian subcontinent (usually with a salwar or churidars or pyjama).

kuru.m: A progressive disease of the central nervous system marked by increasing lack of coordination and advancing to paralysis and death within a year of the appearance of symptoms; thought to have been transmitted by cannibalistic consumption of diseased brain tissue since the disease virtually disappeared when cannibalism was abandoned.

kuvasz.m: Long-established Hungarian breed of tall light-footed but sturdy white dog; used also as a hunting dog.
